steps.text: Whisk balsamic vinegar, oil, salt, and pepper in a small bowl. Pour over tomato slices to marinate.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate.
Mix ground beef, tomato paste, basil, Parmesan cheese, garlic, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper in a large bowl. Form beef mixture into 4 equal patties.

Cook on the preheated grill until the burgers are cooked to your desired degree of doneness, about 5 minutes per side for well done. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read 160 degrees F (70 degrees C). Top each burger with mozzarella cheese; allow to melt. Serve on hamburger buns with marinated tomato slices.

raw_recipe.headline: Caprese Burger
raw_recipe.description: This delicious Caprese burger features fresh basil, marinated tomatoes, and fresh mozzarella atop a ground beef patty. A burst of flavor in every bite!
raw_recipe.name: Caprese Burger

review.reviewBody: Hi everyone! I submitted this recipe and since coming up with it have started to substitute about 1/4 cup storebought pesto for the basil, parm and garlic. It's easier and I think even tastier! The marinated tomatoes are a MUST!

The recipe says nothing about time to marinate the tomato slices, so I assumed it's just however long it takes to prep/cook the burgers -- wrong! Fortunately, I checked other recipes online, and the consensus is to marinate tomatoes at least 2 hours at room temp. With 90 minutes til dinner, I got right on it and the tomatoes turned out fine. Phew! (Spoiler alert: the tomatoes are a huge part of the awesome end product.) Next, I scaled down ingredients for two 1/3lb burgers, mixed as directed, substituting the pesto sauce for basil, garlic and parm. Following others' suggestions, I toasted some ciabatta rolls (lesser buns will not stand up), and prepared a pesto-mayo (1/3c mayo + 2tsp pesto sauce) to spread on the buns. Update: served with Hawaiian Macaroni Salad from this site, and it was the PERFECT side for these burgers! Oh my! This is going to be a regular on the grill this summer. I will allow 2-3 hours for marinating tomatoes, and ciabatta rolls are a MUST, as regular burger rolls will not stand up to this wonderfully juicy creation.

WOW - traditional Italian meets classic American! These flavors combine to make one tasty burger! This is definitely not your average "run of the mill" burger, but something more along the lines of the "gourmet". Be sure to marinate your tomatoes at room temperature. I added some chopped basil to the mix along with a bit of minced garlic. For the meat mixture, I cut back just a bit on the Parmesan cheese and basil and added a bit more tomato paste. If you don't want to add the tomato paste, you could easily sub in some chopped sun-dried tomatoes. Next time, I might add those in anyway because I love 'em! These smelled wonderful on the grill and tasted even better. We served them with a mix of melted mozzarella and provolone along with the tomatoes on toasted crusty Italian rolls - YUM!

Fabulous! As suggested by the lady who posted the recipe, I substituted basil pesto for the fresh basil, Parmesan and garlic. Boy, was that easy. I pan fried these and put the mozzarella on after flipping and cover with a lid to help it melt. Then I served the burger on a ciabatta roll. Yum. Yum.

Delizioso!!! . 

I find your recipe absolutely delightful! I used your suggestion of substituting basil pesto for the basil, parmesan and garlic mixture, another reviewer suggestion of using sun dried tomatoes in lieu of tomato paste and yet another suggestion by another reviewer of using Ciabatta bread which I brushed with a bit of garlic infused extra virgin olive oil and lightly toasted.

I've made the burger now twice and will make it again. Both my family and my boyfriend's family have loved it. I say the toasted ciabatta roll is a must and I also used the tube of basil which I think mixes better then chopped basil and tastes as good. I also used a little garlic powder along with fresh garlic. I had better luck when the meat is really chilled and the patties are made by hand instead of a burger press. When I used the press the burgers fell apart a little.

Wonderful recipe! I like the substitution of basil pesto as well, but either way is perfection. You can also go "vegetarian" and use portobello mushrooms, Remove the gills. Spread the mixture of tomato paste, basil, Parmesan, garlic and pepper on the underside. Preheat the grill to medium. Lightly oil the grill. Cover and grill 15-20 minutes, top with mozzarella, allow to melt and serve topped with marinated tomato.

This is an awesome burger. I used the store bought pesto. 
I also rolled the beef mixture, after adding the pesto and tomato paste, into a "log, then wrapped it in foil and put it in the freezer till it hardened. Then you can slice the burgers into even patty sizes. This is a "gotta repeat" recepie.

You can't go wrong with this flavor combo! Caprese + charcoal-grilled beef = super delish! For a shortcut, I used some of my homemade pesto from the freezer, mixing it into the beef instead of the garlic-basil-tomato paste mixture. So good!

oh my word!
these burgers were so easy to make and the taste was fantabulous!! i used the prepared pesto as suggested, but did add a few leaves of chopped fresh basil for that extra little something to the burger mix. i also added some of the fresh basil to the balsamic marinade. because i live in an apartment, i don't have a grill, so i cooked them in a pan and they came out perfect! i found the recipe for the "best burger sauce" that someone recommended and both my husband and i loved it! we even used it to dip our sweet potato fries that i made with the burgers. this is a keeper and will be made regularly.

This recipe was great. I used Ground chicken instead. It was really great. Also I cooked in a skillet instead of the grill. My husband LOVED it and wants me to make again. Thanks for the recipe.. It ROCKS!!!!

Made this as with ciabatta rolls suggested which I brushed with garlic oil and toasted then spread some pesto mayo on each half. Marinated the tomatoes for a couple hours and added homemade pesto to the ground meat which gave a subtle pesto flavor to the burgers. And a large fresh basil leaf on top of the tomatoes for a nice finish.
Very tasty, and a terrific idea. The entire family loved it.

OMG this is the best. The only thing we did as others suggested was serve on ciabatta buns (which you'll need cause these are juicy) and used a mayo & pesto sauce we did to taste. Will make again for sure. We talked about using a leaner hamburger because it was that juicy, but haven't decided. We prefer the 80/20 because of more flavor in meat. I couldn't really figure out why marinate the tomatoes for 2 hours as suggested but we did & worth it.

The neighbors were out with tongues wagging from the smell from the grill. We prepared these exactly and did not add anything before eating. Needless to say, they went so fast there was no time for a picture. These are tasty, fresh, and perfectly delicious. No more ratty, nasty, plain ones for us! Love this recipe!

Came out fantastic! I usually drizzle olive oil on my burger before putting it on the grill, but this time I used an olive oil and balsamic mixture. I also made a pesto mayo that I put on the ciabatta bun. Definitely making this one again.

Came out fantastic! I usually drizzle olive oil on my burger before putting it on the grill, but this time I used an olive oil and balsamic mixture. I also made a pesto mayo that I put on the ciabatta bun. Definitely making this one again.
Delicious alternative to a classical burger. Definitely lighter with the mozzarella and pesto.
